added_failures_note: the reviewed run recorded no baseline_suite/after_suite arms in its manifest, so no added-failures delta is derivable from this run; 0 is the count of failing ids it recorded, not a measured delta. Its own gate ran 40 passed EXIT=0 at 71d3da6fa over six targeted files, and its red control recorded EXIT=1 with two failing ids at the head arm's own revision.
call_sites: reckon/route_results.py:242 _compute_refresh key rollup (the /_projects/index.json route at reckon/serve.py:2911)

findings.text: follow-on: the landed bar shape makes bar["plan"] the plan's slug string, but the served derived-flow surface still reads it as the embedded inventory row — plan.status, plan.sprint, plan.slug and plan.title at :116-140, item.plan.sprint at :64, item.plan.slug at :67 and :105 — so every bar renders with an undefined href, no title and no sprint chip; the node's brief fenced the SPA to a later node and both the manifest's follow_ons and the fragment record it, so this does not hold the node, but the coordinator must land that SPA node before §6 closes or the crew flow stays degraded.

follow-on: the shipped control test monkeypatches derive_fleet_impl_imputing_effort with its own unweighted sum and then asserts the served row equals that injection, so its assertion holds whatever the production roll-up does and it is not a guard for the roll-up it is named after; the guard is the recorded red run of the real test file (logs/negative_control.log, EXIT=1) plus the 1/15 assertion at :224, and this test should be read as a description of the control rather than as coverage.

follow-on: the bar carries the plan's slug under both "plan" and "slug", stating one value twice in a payload this node shrank so that each bar would stop repeating a row; the two keys will drift unless one is dropped, and the SPA node that resolves the slug against the inventory is the right commit to drop the other.
